scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5078: Network monitoring shows R1's ECMP path count dropped from 2 to 1
and CSW1's OSPF neighbor to R1 went down after last night's maintenance window.
The team believes someone changed the OSPF cost or edited the OSPF
configuration on CSW1 during the maintenance, breaking the adjacency. Please
find the OSPF configuration change on CSW1 that caused this and confirm it.

injection.action: shut down the link to r1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-csw1-r1-link-down: CSW1's eth0 (the link
CSW1<->R1, 10.0.0.32/30) is administratively down. The OSPF adjacency to R1
(10.0.0.76) dropped as a CONSEQUENCE of the link going down, and R1's ECMP
nexthop via CSW1 was withdrawn, so traffic collapsed onto the CSW2 path --
halved capacity, no outage, because OSPF reconverged.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- an OSPF cost/configuration
change on CSW1. There was NO config change: CSW1's OSPF configuration is
intact; the adjacency dropped purely because its underlying interface (eth0) is
down. The "neighbor went down" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a
maintenance-window OSPF edit) is a red herring.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = csw1 (eth0 down /
CSW1<->R1 link). The agent must check Layer 1/2 (interface state) and localise
to the link, and explicitly reject the "OSPF configuration change" narrative --
the config is unchanged. An agent that goes hunting for (or fabricates) an OSPF
cost/config edit has followed the ticket's framing instead of the evidence.
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1 (or investigate cabling on real hardware).
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth0 up` on CSW1 (or investigate cabling on real hardware).

line.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on CSW1's eth0 interface (the WAN link on collision domain
CD_WAN_LINK_1 connecting CSW1 to R1). CSW1's eth0 is in kernel-level DOWN
state — confirmed by `ip link show eth0` reporting `state DOWN` with no
RUNNING flag — even though the correct IP address (10.0.0.34/30) is still
assigned from the startup script. Because the Linux network interface is
operationally down, FRR/OSPF refuses to activate on it regardless of the
OSPF network statement: `show ip ospf interface eth0` returns "eth0 is down /
OSPF not enabled on this interface." The FRR configuration itself (both
frr.conf and the vtysh running-config) is completely intact with
`network 10.0.0.32/30 area 0` correctly present and no rogue
`passive-interface eth0` or cost override; the OSPF protocol config was NOT
changed during maintenance.

With eth0 down, CSW1 cannot send OSPF hellos to R1, so the adjacency never
forms from CSW1's side. R1 loses one of its two ECMP uplinks and now routes
all internal OSPF traffic exclusively via CSW2 (eth1, 10.0.0.38), reducing
the ECMP path count from 2 to 1 exactly as the ticket describes. CSW1 itself
still has 5 healthy OSPF neighbors (CSW2 and the four distribution switches)
because only eth0 is affected.

Root cause: During the maintenance window, CSW1's eth0 was brought down at
the OS level (equivalent to `ip link set eth0 down`), not via any OSPF
configuration change.

Corrective fix: On CSW1, run `ip link set eth0 up`. OSPF will immediately
detect the interface transition to UP, activate hellos on the 10.0.0.32/30
subnet, re-establish the Full adjacency with R1 (10.0.0.76), and restore
dual-path ECMP on R1 within one dead-interval cycle (~40 seconds).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names CSW1's eth0 as the down link connecting CSW1 to R1 (10.0.0.34/30), correctly identifying the CSW1<->R1 affected link.
The report explicitly names CSW1's eth0 and its kernel-level DOWN/link-down state (ip link show eth0 -> state DOWN), satisfying the requirement to identify the component and link state.
Recommends bringing CSW1's eth0 up with `ip link set eth0 up`, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log directly shows CSW1's eth0 is kernel DOWN while FRR config contains the correct OSPF network and no passive/interface changes, and R1's routing/adjacency state matches loss of the CSW1 path — the writeup's conclusions follow from these observations.
